```{r data}
## ---------------------------

# load IPEDS data and merge with the Carnegie Classification

ipeds24 <- read_csv("../data/sources/hd2024.csv")
ipeds_cost <- read_csv("../data/sources/cost1_2024.csv")
#ipeds_schoolsize <- read_csv("../data/sources/ef2024a.csv") #enrollment Fall 2024
carnegie <- read_excel("../data/sources/2025-Public-Data-File.xlsx", sheet = 2)
ic2024 <- read_csv("../data/sources/ic2024.csv")
sfa <- read_csv("../data/sources/sfa2324.csv")
adm <- read_csv("../data/sources/adm2024.csv")
enroll <- read_csv("../data/sources/effy2024.csv") %>%
  filter(EFFYALEV == 3) %>%  #degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates
  select(UNITID, EFFYALEV, EFYTOTLT, EFYAIANT, EFYBKAAT, EFYNHPIT, EFYWHITT, EFYHISPT, EFYASIAT) 
#ipeds_distance <- read_csv("../data/sources/effy2024_dist.csv") %>% 
#  filter(EFFYDLEV == 2) %>%  #undergrad total
#  select(UNITID, EFFYDLEV, EFYDETOT, EFYDEEXC)
ipeds_dist <- read_csv("../data/sources/ef2024a_dist.csv") |> 
  filter(EFDELEV == 2) |>    #undergrad total
  select(UNITID, EFDELEV, EFDETOT, EFDEEXC, XEFDEEXC)
ipeds_learner <- read_csv("../data/sources/ef2024b.csv") |> 
  filter(LSTUDY == 2, EFBAGE %in% c(1, 7)) |>     #undergrad total / all age categories total, age 25 and over total
#number of institutions (= UNITID): 2,487
  select(UNITID, EFBAGE, EFAGE06, EFAGE09) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = EFBAGE, 
              values_from = c(EFAGE06, EFAGE09))


#Let's replace this with the size variable in IPEDS (instsize)
# ipeds_schoolsize <- ipeds_schoolsize |> 
#     filter(EFALEVEL == 1) |> #Level of student (1 == all students total)
#     select(UNITID, EFTOTLT) |> #Grand total

#       EFTOTLT <= 3000 ~ 0,  #small
#       EFTOTLT <= 10000 ~ 1,  #medium
#       EFTOTLT > 10000 ~ 2, #large
#       TRUE ~ NA_real_))

carnegie <- carnegie |> 
  select(unitid, hsi)

# merge files
data <- ipeds24 %>% 
  left_join(carnegie, by = c("UNITID" = "unitid")) %>% 
  left_join(ipeds_cost, by = "UNITID") |> 
  #left_join(ipeds_schoolsize, by = "UNITID") %>%
  left_join(ic2024, by = "UNITID" ) %>%
  left_join(sfa, by = "UNITID") %>%
  left_join(adm, by = "UNITID") %>%
  left_join(enroll, by = "UNITID") |> 
  left_join(ipeds_dist, by = "UNITID") |> 
  left_join(ipeds_learner, by = "UNITID")



# select variables and create a dataset for analysis
x <- data |> 
    rename_all(tolower) |> #converts all column names in a data frame to lowercase
    select(unitid, instnm, city, stabbr, fips, countycd, countynm, cbsa, cbsatype, csa, obereg,
           locale, zip, longitud, latitude, 
           control, iclevel, instcat, deggrant, instsize,
           hloffer,
           carnegieic, carnegiesaec, carnegiealf, carnegieapm, carnegiersch,
           hbcu, hsi, tribal,
           room, relaffil, distnced, athassoc,
           admssn, applcn, openadmp, loan_a, tuition1, upgrntp, 
           efytotlt, efyaiant, efybkaat, efynhpit, efywhitt, efyhispt, efyasiat,
           efdelev, efdetot, efdeexc, xefdeexc, slo7, efage06_1, efage06_7, efage09_1, efage09_7)

# assign to "data"
```

```{r Create Sample}
x <- data %>% 
  filter(fips <= 56) |>                                 # Keep only 50 states and DC
  filter(cbsa != -2) |>                                 # Remove colleges not located in CBSAs 
  # filter(!is.na(control), control != 3) |>            # 3: private for-profit
  filter(!is.na(iclevel), iclevel != 3) |>              # 3: less than 2 years
  filter(!is.na(carnegiealf), carnegiealf != 6) %>%     # 6: graduate-focused
  filter(instcat >= 2 & instcat <= 4)                   # 1: degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees
                                                        # 5-6: non-degree-granting
  #filter(carnegieapm == 1)                             # Keep only colleges classified as "mixed" undergraduate programs
  

data <- x

```


```{r cleaning}
## ---------------------------
##' [Data Cleaning]
## ---------------------------

x <- data |> 
  mutate(
         public = case_when(
            control == 2 ~ 0,                             # 0: private
            control == 1 ~ 1,                             # 1: public 
            control == 3 ~ 2,                             # 2: for-profit
            TRUE ~ NA_real_),   
         
         twoyear = case_when(
            iclevel == 1 ~ 0,                             # 0: 4 or more
            iclevel == 2 ~ 1,                             # 1: at least 2 & less than 4
            TRUE ~ NA_real_),     
         
         # msi = case_when(                                 # 0: non of them
         #    hbcu == 1 ~ 1,                                # 1: HBCU
         #    hsi == 1 ~ 2,                                 # 2: HSI
         #    tribal == 1 ~ 3,                              # 3: TCU
         #    hbcu == 2 & hsi == 0 & tribal == 2 ~ 0,
         #    is.na(hbcu) | is.na(hsi) | is.na(tribal) ~ NA_real_,
         #    TRUE ~ NA_real_),
         
         msi = case_when(
           hbcu == 1 | hsi == 1 | tribal == 1 ~ 1, 
           TRUE ~ 0),
         
         rurality = case_when(
            locale %in% c(31,32,33,41,42,43) ~ 0,         # 0: Town + Rural
            locale %in% c(21,22,23) ~ 1,                  # 1: Suburb
            locale %in% c(11,12,13) ~ 2,                  # 2: City
            TRUE ~ NA_real_),        
         
         rurality = factor(rurality,
                           levels = c(0, 1, 2),
                           labels = c("Town/Rural", "Suburb", "City")),

         size = case_when(
           instsize == 1 ~ 0,                             # 0: < 1,000
           instsize == 2 ~ 1,                             # 1: 1,000 - 4,999
           instsize == 3 ~ 2,                             # 2: 5,000 - 9,999
           instsize == 4 ~ 3,                             # 3: 10,000 - 19,999
           instsize == 5 ~ 4,                             # 4: >=20,000
           TRUE ~ NA_real_),
         
#         tuition = case_when(
#           tuition1 == 0 & obereg != 0 ~ NA_real_,
#           tuition1 == 0 & obereg == 0 ~ 0,
#           tuition1 < 10000 ~ 0,                           # 0: < $10,000          - 1334
#           tuition1 >= 10000 & tuition1 < 20000 ~ 1,       # 1: $10,000 - $19,999  - 689
          # tuition1 >= 20000 & tuition1 < 30000 ~ 2,      # 2: $20,000 - $29,999
#           tuition1 >= 20000 & tuition1 < 40000 ~ 2,       # 3: $30,000 - $39,999  - 531
          # tuition1 >= 40000 & tuition1 < 50000 ~ 4,      # 4: $40,000 - $49,999
#           tuition1 >= 40000                    ~ 3,       # 5: > $50,000          - 384
#           TRUE ~ NA_real_),                               #                       - 316

#         tuitionnn = ntile(tuition1, 4) - 1,               # 0~3: quartiles

#check missing values: sum(is.na(ipeds_cost$TUITION1))  [1] 2,368 (= about 40% of the sample)

         housing = case_when(
           room == 2 ~ 0,                                 # 0: no housing
           room == 1 ~ 1,                                 # 1: offer housing
           TRUE ~ NA_real_),    

         religious = ifelse(relaffil == -2, 0, 1),        # 0: no religious
                                                          # 1: any religious
         
        #We need to remove colleges that offer completely distance education from our sample
         distance = case_when(
           distnced == 2 ~ 0,                             # 0: not completely distanced learning
           distnced == 1 ~ 1,                             # 1: completely distanced learning
           TRUE ~NA_real_),    

         online_perc = case_when(
            is.na(efdetot) ~ NA_real_,
            is.na(efdeexc) & xefdeexc == "A" ~ 0,         # "A": not applicable
            is.na(efdeexc) ~ NA_real_,                    # other missing cases
            TRUE ~ efdeexc / efdetot),

#         online = case_when(
#            is.na(online_perc) ~ NA_real_,
#            online_perc == 0 ~ 0,                         # none                        - 860
#            online_perc < 0.25 ~ 1,                       # more than 0%, less than 25% - 1588
#            online_perc < 0.50 ~ 2,                       # 25% to less than 50%        - 717
#            online_perc <= 1 ~ 3,                         # 50% to 100%                 - 288
#            TRUE ~ NA_real_),                             # NA                          - 11

        online = ntile(online_perc, 4) - 1,               # 0~3: quartiles

#check missing values: sum(is.na(ipeds_dist$EFDETOT))  [1] 0

        evening = case_when(
          slo7 == 0 ~ 0,                                  # 0: no weekend/evening courses
          slo7 == 1 ~ 1,                                  # 1: allows classes only on weekends or only in evenings
          TRUE ~ NA_real_),

#check missing values: sum(is.na(ic2024$SLO7))  [1] 0
        
#        adult_perc = case_when(
#            is.na(efage09_7) ~ NA_real_,
#            is.na(efage09_1) ~ NA_real_,
#            TRUE ~ efage09_7 / efage09_1),
        
#        adult_perc = case_when(
#            is.na(efage09_7) ~ NA_real_,
#            is.na(efage09_1) ~ NA_real_,
#            TRUE ~ efage09_7 / efage09_1),

#        adult = ntile(adult_perc, 4) - 1,                 # 0~3: quartiles

#check missing values: sum(is.na(ipeds_learner$EFAGE09_1))  [1] 0
#check missing values: sum(is.na(ipeds_learner$EFAGE09_7))  [1] 9

#        parttime_perc = case_when(
#            is.na(efage06_1) ~ NA_real_,
#            is.na(efage09_1) ~ NA_real_,
#            TRUE ~ efage06_1 / efage09_1),

#        parttime = case_when(
#            is.na(parttime_perc) ~ NA_real_,
#            parttime_perc == 0 ~ 0,                       # none                        - 73
#            parttime_perc < 0.25 ~ 1,                     # more than 0%, less than 25% - 828
#            parttime_perc < 0.50 ~ 2,                     # 25% to less than 50%        - 344
#            parttime_perc <= 1 ~ 3,                       # 50% to 100%                 - 769
#            TRUE ~ NA_real_),                             # NA                          - 1450

#         parttime = ntile(parttime_perc, 4) - 1,          # 0~3: quartiles        
#check missing values: sum(is.na(ipeds_learner$EFAGE06_1))  [1] 0

         sports = case_when(
           athassoc == 2 ~ 0,                             # 0: not a member
           athassoc == 1 ~ 1,                             # 1: member of National Athletic Association
           TRUE ~NA_real_),

         loan = case_when(
           is.na(loan_a) ~ NA_real_,
           loan_a <= quantile(loan_a, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE) ~ 0,     # 0: lowest
           loan_a <= quantile(loan_a, 0.50, na.rm = TRUE) ~ 1,     # 1: low 
           loan_a <= quantile(loan_a, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE) ~ 2,     # 2: high
           TRUE ~ 3),                                              # 3: highest
 
# Q. Since MLCA requires variables starting at 0, is it appropriate to divide loan amount into quartiles (0–3)?

         asc = case_when(
           carnegiesaec == 2 ~ 0,                         # 0: Higher Access, Lower Earnings 
           carnegiesaec == 4 ~ 1,                         # 1: Higher Access, Medium Earnings
           carnegiesaec == 6 ~ 2,                         # 2: Higher Access, Higher Earnings
           carnegiesaec == 1 ~ 3,                         # 3: Lower Access, Lower Earnings
           carnegiesaec == 3 ~ 4,                         # 4: Lower Access, Medium Earnings
           carnegiesaec == 5 ~ 5,                         # 5: Lower Access, Higher Earnings
           TRUE ~ NA_real_),

         awardlev = case_when(
           carnegiealf %in% c(1,2) ~ 0,                    # 0: associates 
           carnegiealf == 3 ~ 1,                            # 1: baccalaureate
           carnegiealf == 4 ~ 2,                           # 2: undergrad / grad-Master's
           carnegiealf == 5 ~ 3,                           # 3: undergrad / grad-Doctorate 
           
           is.na(carnegiealf) & (hloffer == 3 | hloffer == 4) ~ 0,
           carnegiealf == -2 & (hloffer == 3 | hloffer == 4) ~ 0,
           hloffer == 5 & instcat == 2 ~ 1,
           
           TRUE ~ NA_real_),
         #Check: x %>% filter(is.na(awardlev)) %>% View()

         focus = case_when(
            carnegieapm == -2                          ~ 0,  # 0: Not classified
            carnegieapm == 1                           ~ 1,  # 1: Mixed
            carnegieapm == 2                           ~ 2,  # 2: Professions-focused
            carnegieapm == 3                           ~ 3,  # 3: Applied and career studies
            carnegieapm %in% c(4,5)                    ~ 4,  # 4: Arts and sciences
            carnegieapm == 6                           ~ 5,  # 5: Business
            carnegieapm %in% c(8,9,10)                 ~ 6,  # 6: Medical sciences/health
            carnegieapm == 11                          ~ 7,  # 7: STEM
            carnegieapm == 12                          ~ 8,  # 8: Theology
            TRUE ~ NA_real_),                         
        
        research = case_when( 
            carnegiersch == -2 ~ 0,                   #0: No research designation
            carnegiersch == 3 ~ 1,                    #1: Research Colleges and Universities 
            carnegiersch == 2 ~ 2,                    #2: High Spending
            carnegiersch == 1 ~ 3,                    #3: Very High Spending  
            TRUE ~ NA_real_),          
         
         cbsa = as.character(cbsa),

         cbsatype = case_when(
           cbsatype == 2 ~ 0,   # Micropolitan
           cbsatype == 1 ~ 1,   # Metropolitan
           TRUE ~ NA_real_),


        pell = case_when(
          upgrntp < 10                   ~ 0,
          upgrntp >= 10 & upgrntp < 30   ~ 1,
          #upgrntp >= 20 & upgrntp < 30   ~ 2,
          upgrntp >= 30 & upgrntp < 50   ~ 2,
         # upgrntp >= 40 & upgrntp < 50   ~ 4,
          upgrntp >= 50                  ~ 3,
          TRUE ~ NA_real_)
          
       )


data <- x |>
  filter(distance == 0) %>%                       # remove observations with only distance education
  group_by(cbsa) %>% 
  mutate(inst_num = n_distinct(unitid),
         inst_num = as.numeric(inst_num)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(admrate = admssn/applcn) %>% 
  # mutate(admrate = if_else(openadmp == 1, 1, admrate)) |> 
  mutate(selectivity = case_when(
         openadmp == 1 ~ 0,
         admrate == 1 ~ 0,                        #0: open 
         admrate >= 0.75 & admrate < 1 ~ 1,       #1: less selective
         admrate >= 0.40 & admrate < 0.75 ~ 2,    #2: selective
         admrate < 0.40 ~ 3,                      #3: more selective
         TRUE ~ NA_real_),
         
         i_perc_black = efybkaat/efytotlt,              #Percent of degree-seeking undergrads by race/ethnicity
         i_perc_white = efywhitt/efytotlt,
         i_perc_hisp = efyhispt/efytotlt,
         i_perc_nhpi = (efyaiant + efynhpit)/efytotlt,
         i_perc_asian = efyasiat/efytotlt,
         i_perc_nonwhite = 1 - i_perc_white,
         nonwhite = ntile(i_perc_nonwhite, 4),
         nonwhite = nonwhite - 1
         ) %>% 
  rename(region = obereg) %>% 
  mutate(cbsa = as.character(cbsa))
  
```


```{r}
z <- read_csv("../data/sources/effy2024.csv") %>% 
  filter(EFFYLEV == 2 | EFFYLEV == 4) %>% 
  select(UNITID, EFFYALEV, EFYTOTLT) %>% 
  mutate(EFFYALEV = if_else(EFFYALEV == 2, "undergrad", "grad")) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = "UNITID",
              names_from = EFFYALEV, 
              values_from = EFYTOTLT) %>% 
  mutate(total_pop = undergrad + grad,
         per_undergrad = undergrad/total_pop,
         per_grad = grad/total_pop)
```

```{r census/ACS data}
#| output: false


## ---------------------------
## [Census/ACS Data]
## ---------------------------


land_area <- core_based_statistical_areas(
  cb = TRUE, 
  year = 2024) %>% 
  select(GEOID, ALAND)


census <- get_acs(geography = "cbsa",
                  year = 2024,
                  variables = c("B01003_001E", # Total population
                                "B19013_001E", # Median Household Income in the Past 12 Months
                                "DP03_0119PE", # % families below poverty line
                                "DP03_0005PE", # % unemployed over 16 years old
                                "DP02_0068PE", # % bach or higher
                                "B03002_003E", # total white (alone, not hispanic)
                                "B03002_004E", # total black (alone, not hispanic)
                                "B03002_012E", # total hispanic
                                "B03002_006E", # total asian (alone, not hispanic)
                                "B03002_001E"  # total by ethnicity
                  ),
                  output = "wide") %>% 
  left_join(land_area)


census <- census |>
  mutate(perc_white = B03002_003E/B03002_001E*100,
         perc_black = B03002_004E/B03002_001E*100,
         perc_hisp = B03002_012E/B03002_001E*100,
         perc_asian = B03002_006E/B03002_001E*100,
         tot_pop = B01003_001E/100000,
         pop_density = B01003_001E/(ALAND/2589988.10)) |> #population per sq mile
  rename(perc_ba = DP02_0068PE,
         med_income = B19013_001E,
         perc_pov = DP03_0119PE,
         perc_unemployed = DP03_0005PE) |> 
  select(tot_pop, pop_density, perc_ba,
         med_income, perc_pov, perc_unemployed,
         perc_white, perc_black, perc_hisp, perc_asian,
         GEOID) |> 
  mutate(GEOID = as.character(GEOID))

data <- data |>
  left_join(census, by = c("cbsa" = "GEOID"))
```

```{r MCLA setup}

# Variables:
#   Y-        Columns with indicator variables for level 1 class membership (predictors of institution-level classes)
                # public, two_year, size, msi, award level, research, selectivity 
              
#   iT-       Number of lower-level latent classes

#   id_high-  Name of column with higher-level id
                # CBSA

#   iM-       Number of higher-level latent classes

#   Z-        Columns with lower-level covariates (predictors of level 1 class membership)
                # rurality, housing, religious, sports

#   Zh-       Columns with higher-level covariates (predictors of level 2 class membership)
                # Variables- region, number of IHEs, total population, percent bachelors degree, median income, percent poverty, percent white, percent black, percent hispanic, percent asian


# Level-1 indicators: Observed institution characteristics used to define the latent institution classes
# Level-1 covariates: Institution-level predictors that explain class membership
# Level-2 covariates: CBSA-level regional variables that explain differences in institution class probabilities across regions


# Lower-level indicators based on framework for insitutional diversity in: 
# Harris, M.S. An Empirical Typology of the Institutional Diversity of U.S. Colleges and Universities. Innov High Educ 45, 183–199 (2020). https://doi.org/10.1007/s10755-019-09494-6

#indicators
Y <- c(
  #systemic- structural and governance characteristics
  "public", "size", #"twoyear",
  
  #programmatic- degree level and academic disciplinary offerings
  "awardlev", "focus", "research",
  
  #procedural- how programs are offered and implemented (Harris included % of students enrolled in distance-only classes, and we include that in this analysis)
            #-the institution / management? operation?
  "online",  #ADD VARIABLE FOR THE PERCENTAGE OF STUDENTS WHO ARE EXCLUSIVELY ENROLLED IN ONLINE COURSES
             #categorized share of undergraduates enrolled exclusively in distance education
  "evening",
#  "tuitionnn",
#(1)including tuition as quartiles: iT= 8 & iM= 2            (#obs = 1779)
#(2)including tuition & parttime quartiles: iT= 8 & iM= 2    (#obs = 1779)
  
  #constituential- "student demographics, background, preparation, and abilities" (Harris, 2020 p.187)
  "selectivity", "pell", "msi", "nonwhite" #, "adult", "parttime"
  ) #level-1 indicators 

Z <- c("i_perc_white", "i_perc_black", "i_perc_hisp", "i_perc_asian", "housing", "rurality", "religious")       #level-1 covariates   "sports", 

Zh <- c("cbsatype", "inst_num", "tot_pop", "pop_density", "perc_ba", "med_income", "perc_pov", "perc_unemployed", "perc_white", "perc_black", "perc_hisp", "perc_asian")   #level-2 covariates  "metropolitan", "region", 



```


```{r descriptive statistics}

## ---------------------------
## Descriptive Statistics
## ---------------------------


# ---------------------------
# Level 1: Institution-level variables
# ---------------------------

# Categorical Level-1 variables
l1_cat <- c("public", "size", "awardlev", "focus", "research", "evening", 
            "selectivity", "pell", "msi", "housing", "rurality", "religious")


# Continuous Level-1 variables
l1_cont <- c("online_perc", "i_perc_nonwhite", "i_perc_white", 
             "i_perc_black", "i_perc_hisp", "i_perc_asian")


# Proportion for categorical variables
l1_categorical_desc <- data_mlca |>
  select(all_of(l1_cat)) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(),
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "Category") |>
  count(Variable, Category, name = "N") |>
  group_by(Variable) |>
  mutate(Proportion = N / sum(N)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(Variable, Category, Proportion) |>
  mutate(Proportion = round(Proportion, 2))

l1_categorical_desc


# Mean, SD for continuous variables
l1_continuous_desc <- data_mlca |>
  summarise(across(all_of(l1_cont),
      list(Mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
           SD   = ~sd(., na.rm = TRUE)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = c("Variable", ".value"),
               names_pattern = "(.+)_(Mean|SD)$") |>
  mutate(across(c(Mean, SD), ~round(., 2)))

l1_continuous_desc



# ---------------------------
# Level 2: CBSA-level variables
# ---------------------------

# Keep one observation per CBSA
cbsa_data <- data_mlca |>
  distinct(cbsa_id, .keep_all = TRUE)


# Categorical Level-2 variable
l2_categorical_desc <- cbsa_data |>
  count(cbsatype, name = "N") |>
  mutate(Proportion = N / sum(N)) |>
  select(cbsatype, Proportion) |>
  mutate(Proportion = round(Proportion, 2))

l2_categorical_desc


# Continuous Level-2 variables
l2_cont <- c("inst_num", "tot_pop", "pop_density", "perc_ba",
             "med_income", "perc_pov", "perc_unemployed",
             "perc_white", "perc_black", "perc_hisp", "perc_asian")


l2_continuous_desc <- cbsa_data |>
  summarise(across(all_of(l2_cont),
                   list(Mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
                        SD   = ~sd(., na.rm = TRUE)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = c("Variable", ".value"),
               names_pattern = "(.+)_(Mean|SD)$") |>
  mutate(across(c(Mean, SD), ~round(., 2)))

l2_continuous_desc



# ---------------------------
# Sample sizes
# ---------------------------

sample_sizes <- tibble(
  Level = c("Institutions", "CBSAs"),
  N = c(nrow(data_mlca), nrow(cbsa_data)))

sample_sizes



# ---------------------------
# Save descriptive statistics
# ---------------------------

write_xlsx(list("L1 categorical" = l1_categorical_desc,
                "L1 continuous"  = l1_continuous_desc,
                "L2 categorical" = l2_categorical_desc,
                "L2 continuous"  = l2_continuous_desc,
                "Sample sizes"    = sample_sizes),
           "../data/MLCA_ds.xlsx")

```


```{r multicollinearity}
# Level-1 indicators (Y)
## cf. these are not predictors, so technically we don't need to check for multicollinearity here
## cf. these are categorical variables, so VIF may not be appropriate
y_data <- data_mlca |> select(all_of(Y))

set.seed(1234)
y_data$dummy_y <- rnorm(nrow(y_data))

vif_y_model <- lm(dummy_y ~ ., data = y_data)
vif(vif_y_model)


# Level-1 covariates (Z)
z_data <- data_mlca |>  
  select(all_of(Z))

set.seed(1234)
z_data$dummy_y <- rnorm(nrow(z_data))

vif_z_model <- lm(dummy_y ~ ., data = z_data)
vif(vif_z_model)


# Level-2 covariates (Zh)
zh_data <- data_mlca |>  
  select(all_of(Zh)) |>  
  mutate(cbsatype = as.factor(cbsatype))   # switch nominal variable to factor

zh_data$dummy_y <- rnorm(nrow(zh_data))

vif_zh_model <- lm(dummy_y ~ ., data = zh_data)
vif(vif_zh_model)


```


```{r mlca}
set.seed(1234)

model_selection <- multiLCA(
  data = data_mlca,
  Y              = Y,
  iT             = 6:15,
  Z              = Z,
  iM             = 2:8,
  id_high        = c("cbsa_id"),
  Zh             = Zh,
  incomplete     = FALSE,
  extout         = TRUE,
  verbose        = TRUE,
  sequential     = TRUE,
  reord          = FALSE
)

analytic_model <- model_selection

# analytic_model
```

```r optimal 12/6
#|eval: false

# This is the actual 12/6 model with Level-1 and Level-2 covariates, but it currently returns a "solve(): solution not found" error

set.seed(1234)

analytic_model <- multiLCA(

analytic_model
```

```{r level 1 post-estimation}

# mPi: lower-level class proportions/probabilities ("How prevalent is each L1 class?")
# mPhi: item-response probabilities conditional on L1 class ("What does each institution class look like?")
# mPMsumX: posterior probabilities of L1 class membership, marginalized over L2 classes ("Which L1 class is each institution most likely to belong to?")
# mPW: posterior probabilities of L2 class membership ("Which L2 cluster is each CBSA most likely to belong to?")



## ---------------------------
## Level 1 post-estimation
## ---------------------------

# lower-level class proportions
l1_proportions <- as.data.frame(analytic_model$mPi)

# item-response probabilities
l1_probabilities <- as.data.frame(analytic_model$mPhi)

# Posterior-probability columns only
# mPMsumX also contains original data columns when dataout = TRUE,
# so retain only columns corresponding to the Level-1 latent classes.
l1_posterior <- as.data.frame(
  analytic_model$mPMsumX[, colnames(analytic_model$mPhi), drop = FALSE]
)

# sanity checks
stopifnot(nrow(l1_posterior) == nrow(data_mlca))
stopifnot(ncol(l1_posterior) == ncol(analytic_model$mPhi))

# predicted Level-1 class
l1_classes <- data_mlca |>
  select(unitid, instnm, cbsa, cbsa_id) |>
  mutate(
    L1_Predicted_Class = max.col(
      as.matrix(l1_posterior),
      ties.method = "first"),
    L1_Max_Probability = apply(l1_posterior, 1, max))

# institutions sorted by predicted class
l1_institutions_by_class <- l1_classes |>
  arrange(L1_Predicted_Class, instnm)

# count institutions in each predicted Level-1 class
l1_class_counts <- l1_classes |>
  count(L1_Predicted_Class, name = "N_Institutions")

l1_class_counts

```


```{r level 2 predicted clusters}

# vU_modal: vector of posterior modal class assignments (the class with the highest posterior probability)
# vU_modal is available for some model specifications, but is not provided as the relevant Level-2 assignment output here.
# For the multilevel model, modal assignments can be obtained from:
#   mPMsumX -> predicted L1 class for each institution
#   mPW     -> predicted L2 cluster for each CBSA



## ---------------------------
## Level 2 predicted clusters
## ---------------------------

# posterior probabilities of Level-2 cluster membership
l2_posterior <- as.data.frame(analytic_model$mPW)

# sanity check: number of posterior rows should equal number of CBSAs
stopifnot(nrow(l2_posterior) == n_distinct(data_mlca$cbsa_id))

# sanity check2: number of posterior rows should equal number of CBSA IDs
stopifnot(setequal(as.character(row.names(analytic_model$mPW)), unique(as.character(data_mlca$cbsa_id))))

# assign each CBSA to the cluster with the highest posterior probability
l2_clusters <- data.frame(
  cbsa_id = row.names(analytic_model$mPW),
  L2_Predicted_Class = max.col(as.matrix(l2_posterior), ties.method = "first"),
  L2_Max_Probability = apply(l2_posterior, 1, max),
  
# posterior probability for each Level-2 cluster
  Cluster1 = l2_posterior[, 1],
  Cluster2 = l2_posterior[, 2],
  Cluster3 = l2_posterior[, 3],
  Cluster4 = l2_posterior[, 4],
  Cluster5 = l2_posterior[, 5],
  Cluster6 = l2_posterior[, 6]
)


# CBSA-level data: one row per CBSA
cbsa_level_data <- data_mlca |>
  mutate(cbsa_id = as.character(cbsa_id)) |>
  distinct(cbsa_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(cbsa_id, cbsa,
         all_of(setdiff(Zh, "inst_num")))

# number of institutions actually included in the analytic sample
cbsa_inst_counts <- data_mlca |>
  mutate(cbsa_id = as.character(cbsa_id)) |>
  count(cbsa_id, name = "N_Institutions_CBSA")

# attach CBSA characteristics and analytic-sample institution counts
l2_clusters <- l2_clusters |>
  left_join(cbsa_level_data, by = "cbsa_id") |>
  left_join(cbsa_inst_counts, by = "cbsa_id")

# count number of CBSAs and institutions in each predicted Level-2 cluster
l2_cluster_counts <- l2_clusters |>
  group_by(L2_Predicted_Class) |>
  summarise(
    N_CBSAs = n(),
    N_Institutions = sum(N_Institutions_CBSA),
    .groups = "drop")

l2_cluster_counts

# sanity checks
stopifnot(sum(l2_cluster_counts$N_CBSAs) == 725)
stopifnot(sum(l2_cluster_counts$N_Institutions) == 3133)



## ---------------------------
## Level 2 multinomial logistic regression
## ---------------------------

# Create predicted Level-2 cluster assignment from posterior probabilities
reg_data <- l2_clusters |>
  select(cbsa_id, L2_Predicted_Class, L2_Max_Probability) |>
  mutate(
    cbsa_id = as.character(cbsa_id),
    pred_class2 = paste0("G", L2_Predicted_Class)
  ) |>
  select(cbsa_id, pred_class2, L2_Max_Probability) |>
  right_join(
    data_mlca |>
      mutate(cbsa_id = as.character(cbsa_id)),
    by = "cbsa_id"
  )

# Make Cluster 1 the reference category
reg_data <- reg_data |>
  mutate(
    pred_class2 = factor(
      pred_class2,
      levels = paste0("G", 1:6)
    )
  )

# Multinomial logistic regression
reg_model <- vglm(
  pred_class2 ~
    cbsatype + inst_num + tot_pop + pop_density +
    perc_ba + med_income + perc_pov + perc_unemployed +
    perc_white + perc_black + perc_hisp + perc_asian,
  data = reg_data,
  family = multinomial(refLevel = 1)
)

summary(reg_model)


## ---------------------------
## Extract coefficients
## ---------------------------

coef_vec <- coef(reg_model)
vc <- vcov(reg_model)
se_vec <- sqrt(diag(vc))

apa_table <- data.frame(
  term = names(coef_vec),
  estimate = coef_vec,
  SE = se_vec,
  z = coef_vec / se_vec,
  p = 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(coef_vec / se_vec))),
  OR = exp(coef_vec),
  CI_low = exp(coef_vec - 1.96 * se_vec),
  CI_high = exp(coef_vec + 1.96 * se_vec)
) |>
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      p < .001 ~ "***",
      p < .01  ~ "**",
      p < .05  ~ "*",
      TRUE     ~ ""
    ),
    Est = paste0(sprintf("%.3f", estimate), sig),
    SE_display = sprintf("%.3f", SE),
    OR = round(OR, 3),
    CI = paste0(
      "[",
      round(CI_low, 3),
      ", ",
      round(CI_high, 3),
      "]"
    )
  )

apa_table


## ---------------------------
## Reshape for Table 6
## ---------------------------

reg_long <- apa_table |>
  rownames_to_column("row_id") |>
  mutate(
    Comparison = str_extract(term, "(?<=:)[0-9]+$"),
    Predictor = str_remove(term, ":[0-9]+$"),
    Cluster = as.integer(Comparison) + 1
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cluster)) |>
  select(Predictor, Cluster, Est, SE_display)

reg_table <- reg_long |>
  mutate(
    Cluster = paste0("Cluster_", Cluster)
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Cluster,
    values_from = c(Est, SE_display),
    names_glue = "{Cluster}_{.value}"
  ) |>
  select(
    Predictor,
    Cluster_2_Est, Cluster_2_SE_display,
    Cluster_3_Est, Cluster_3_SE_display,
    Cluster_4_Est, Cluster_4_SE_display,
    Cluster_5_Est, Cluster_5_SE_display,
    Cluster_6_Est, Cluster_6_SE_display
  )

institution_row <- tibble(
  Predictor = "N Institutions",
  Cluster_2_Est = as.character(
    l2_cluster_counts$N_Institutions[
      l2_cluster_counts$L2_Predicted_Class == 2
    ]
  ),
  Cluster_2_SE_display = "",

  Cluster_3_Est = as.character(
    l2_cluster_counts$N_Institutions[
      l2_cluster_counts$L2_Predicted_Class == 3
    ]
  ),
  Cluster_3_SE_display = "",

  Cluster_4_Est = as.character(
    l2_cluster_counts$N_Institutions[
      l2_cluster_counts$L2_Predicted_Class == 4
    ]
  ),
  Cluster_4_SE_display = "",

  Cluster_5_Est = as.character(
    l2_cluster_counts$N_Institutions[
      l2_cluster_counts$L2_Predicted_Class == 5
    ]
  ),
  Cluster_5_SE_display = "",

  Cluster_6_Est = as.character(
    l2_cluster_counts$N_Institutions[
      l2_cluster_counts$L2_Predicted_Class == 6
    ]
  ),
  Cluster_6_SE_display = ""
)

reg_table <- bind_rows(
  reg_table,
  institution_row
)

reg_table

```



```{r Save}

## ---------------------------
## Save post-estimation outputs
## ---------------------------

# Level 1: institution assignments by predicted class
write_csv(
  l1_institutions_by_class,
  "../data_paper2/l1_institutions_by_class.csv"
)

# Level 2: CBSA and institution counts by predicted cluster
write_csv(
  l2_cluster_counts,
  "../data_paper2/l2_cluster_counts.csv"
)

# Level 2: final regression table
write_csv(
  reg_table,
  "../data_paper2/table6_multinomial_regression.csv"
)



```
